areas.label: Data governance
areas.desc: Who decides about data, and how: ownership, stewardship, policy, ethics and maturity. DAMA puts it at the centre of the wheel because it steers every other area.

areas.label: Data architecture
areas.desc: The overall design of an organisation's data estate: platforms, lakes, meshes and the blueprints that connect them.

areas.label: Data modelling and design
areas.desc: Describing what data means and how it fits together: models, schemas and ontologies.

areas.label: Data storage and operations
areas.desc: Running the databases and stores that hold data: provisioning, migration, backup and performance.

areas.label: Data security and privacy
areas.desc: Keeping data safe and lawful: protecting personal data, pseudonymising, controlling access and creating safe synthetic data.

caps.label: Trusted research and secure data environments

areas.label: Data integration and interoperability
areas.desc: Moving and combining data between systems: pipelines, orchestration, transformation, streaming and exchange.

areas.label: Document and content management
areas.desc: Looking after documents, records and web content, including archives and digital preservation.

areas.label: Reference and master data
areas.desc: Shared lists and records everyone should agree on: code lists, registers, addresses and organisations, and matching records about the same thing.

areas.label: Data warehousing and business intelligence
areas.desc: Bringing data together for analysis and decisions: warehouses, dashboards, reports and analytical publishing.

areas.label: Metadata management
areas.desc: Describing data so it can be found, understood and trusted: catalogues, dictionaries, lineage and metadata standards.

areas.label: Data quality
areas.desc: Whether data is fit for use: profiling it, testing it against rules, monitoring it over time, and fixing it.
